publisher: Act No. 111/1998 Coll. on Higher Education Institutions (consolidated text on zakonyprolidi.cz)
claim: The Higher Education Act divides vysoké školy into university-type (univerzitní) and non-university-type (neuniverzitní) institutions; section 48(4)(c), in force since 1 March 2025, accepts the International Baccalaureate as proof of completed secondary education for bachelor's admission; section 58 lets public institutions charge fees for study in a foreign language.
excerpt: § 48(4): … prokazuje splnění podmínky dosažení středního vzdělání s maturitní zkouškou … c) dokladem o udělení Mezinárodního bakalaureátu, vydaným International Baccalaureate světovou školou
interpretation: The IB exemption means no nostrification. Study in Czech at a public institution is free; the fee depends on the language of instruction, not on nationality.

attestation.note: Czech statute on a private consolidation site (zakonyprolidi.cz). On 2026-09-24 the Central Europe and Baltics audit pass read § 48(4) in the raw Czech text and recorded the excerpt above; §§ 2 and 58 were not re-read and a person should still check them in Czech. The Czech ministry pages that might describe the sector (msmt.gov.cz 'Study in Czech Republic', 'Brochure on the Czech Higher Education System') returned 'Stránka nenalezena' on 2026-09-23.

claim: Charles University accepts an IB Diploma submitted after 1 March 2025 automatically, without an assessment fee.
excerpt: If applicants choose the option of proving the fulfilment of the admission requirement by submitting an IB diploma after 1 March 2025, the document will be automatically accepted by the faculty in the admission procedure without an assessment fee being charged.
interpretation: The largest university confirming the statutory exemption in practice. Other universities may still charge a verification fee (Masaryk does, per the country profile).

publisher: Study in Czechia (Czech National Agency for International Education and Research)
claim: There is no central application for Czech universities; each application is submitted and paid for separately, and September-start deadlines usually fall between February and April.
excerpt: There is no single central application form for all Czech universities. […] Each application is usually submitted and paid for separately. […] The application deadline is usually between February and April.

publisher: Study in Czechia (Czech National Agency for International Education and Research)
claim: Public and state higher education institutions offer tuition-free programmes taught in Czech, regardless of nationality.
excerpt: Public and state higher education institutions in Czechia offer tuition-free degree programmes taught in Czech, regardless of nationality.
interpretation: The page does not state English-taught fees; those are set per university.

claim: Masaryk University application windows for September entry are set per faculty: Faculty of Science bachelor's 1 November–28 February; Faculty of Informatics 15 December–30 April.
excerpt: Submit your application during this period: 1 November–28 February […] Submit your application during this period: 15 December–30 April
interpretation: The page carries no year, so the route reads these windows onto the 2027 intake and marks them provisional. Shows how much the date depends on the faculty, not just the university.

attestation.note: No academic-year heading on the page.
